title: His father Francis Watkins and barbershop quartet songs
summary: His father sang bass in a barbershop quartet, and Watkins began singing only with Lewis around 1946.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What about your daddy? What was his name? Well my father, Francis Watkins. And did he sing any special songs?

Well they had them old time barbershop songs they used to sing. And just like I said, I didn't start doing any vocalizing until I started playing with George around 1946. And the first time I was taking a chance I was singing anything. Seemed as though I was doing pretty good so I started buying up copies of different songs and would mark them down in my books so I could read them off. You know when it comes time for me to sing. I've been singing vocals ever since. I've been singing vocals ever since.
You don't remember the names of any barbershop songs you daddy told?

Let's see they used to sing Sweet Emma Liner my gal. I love them old songs they used to sing. Sweet out of line. Sweet out of line. All the old time songs they had back around them times. They're about the best quartet they had back in the whole city. Who were the guys that he was singing with? Sweet Out of Line, all the old times songs they had back around them times. They're about the best quartet they had back in the whole city.
Who were the guys that he was singing with? Did you know them?
Oh, I can't recall their names now, no. I really can't recall their names.
